As the premier ⟦0⟧ nation in 1936, the Soviet Union is the head of the Comintern, consisting of ⟦1⟧ and ⟦2⟧. Meanwhile, ⟦3⟧, and ⟦4⟧ are the only other countries that have a favorable view of the USSR.
Should ⟦0⟧ prevail in the Spanish Civil War, it may be amenable to joining, as would a communist-aligned ⟦1⟧.

While led by ⟦0⟧ (the Centre path), the ⟦1⟧ runs a hidden ⟦2⟧ meter from 0 to 100, shown in its own interface. It represents Stalin's distrust of the party and the armed forces and drives the purges that periodically remove the country's characters (generals, admirals, advisors and theorists). The meter starts at 0 and is tied to the ⟦3⟧ national spirit ( gain ⟦4⟧, ⟦5⟧).

⟦0⟧ — Paranoia rises every week from active modifiers, chiefly Stalin's own ⟦1⟧ trait and the current head of the NKVD. The base weekly increase is small (+1 per active modifier), but replacing Genrikh Yagoda with Nikolai Yezhov raises the weekly gain (and lowers stability further).
⟦0⟧ apply one-off changes in discrete steps: ⟦1⟧, ⟦2⟧, ⟦3⟧, ⟦4⟧, ⟦5⟧. The value is clamped to 0–100.
The player can push Paranoia back down through purges, forged production reports and certain decisions.
Occasional ⟦0⟧ — one or a few random characters are lost.
High alert. ⟦0⟧ can fire, removing a larger batch of characters.

Each week the game rolls for a purge, weighted by how many days that week were spent at medium versus high Paranoia — the more days at high Paranoia, the likelier a Great Purge over a Regular one. After any purge there is a ⟦0⟧ before another can occur.

Independently of the random meter, four focuses on the Centre path (⟦0⟧, ⟦1⟧, ⟦2⟧ and ⟦3⟧) each trigger an unavoidable Great Purge — detailed under ⟦4⟧. Characters already killed by the random Paranoia system are skipped and replaced, so the total number purged cannot be reduced; only ⟦5⟧ characters die changes.
The Bloc of Rights and Trotskyites

If the player is following an Opposition path to depose Stalin and Paranoia climbs above 89, each day carries a ⟦0⟧ to immediately ignite the Soviet Civil War (the AI is exempt from this check). Keeping Paranoia low — or finishing the coup quickly — is therefore essential on the Right and Left Opposition routes. The war itself is covered in ⟦1⟧ below.

The Soviet Civil War is fired by the political focus tree when an Opposition faction moves against Stalin. The player always leads the rebels; Stalin's loyalists break away as a new country, the ⟦0⟧ (tag SOS), keeping Moscow as their capital. Stalin leads SOS (or Lavrenty Beriya if Stalin is already dead), and the Stalinist side instantly completes the ⟦1⟧ focuses.
A normal civil war splits forces roughly government alignment. The Soviet war instead splits them by how much of the state and armed forces the Opposition has won over in advance through its focuses:

Each branch — army, navy and air — has its own "opposition support" value, raised by the focuses that align commanders and units to your cause. With no preparation it bottoms out at a 20% floor for that branch and is capped at 90%; the Stalinist SOS keeps the remainder. (An AI-led Opposition gets +25% to any branch below 55%.)

Separately, the Opposition's popular support feeds a dynamic modifier (⟦0⟧), active for the whole war, that shifts the surrender surrender limit in the rebels' favour and against Stalin in proportion to that support.

The officer corps is not divided evenly. The rebels keep only the commanders they have aligned to their faction; every other general and admiral — including all unaligned officers — defects to Stalin's SOS, which additionally receives every Stalinist-aligned officer.

⟦0⟧ keeps Trotskyist-aligned commanders — notably ⟦1⟧ and ⟦2⟧, won over by the ⟦3⟧ and ⟦4⟧ focuses (plus a few randomly converted generals). Because this path protects them instead of purging them, Tukhachevsky and Primakov — historically shot in 1937 — survive and fight for you.

⟦0⟧ keep monarchist-sympathizer commanders and additionally raise unique White formations from their focuses: "Ruki" (Hands) NKVD infantry from ⟦1⟧, "Rebyata" youth units, "Stariki" (Old Guard) cavalry, returning Cossack/Manchurian cavalry, and Ataman Grigory Semyonov transferred from the Far East.
During the war, a monthly event lets Stalinist generals who were merely ⟦0⟧ into loyalty defect to the Opposition (≈25% chance each), slowly evening the rosters.

The Exiles path in particular destabilises the union: from the third month onward a monthly check can spawn breakaway nations — ⟦0⟧, ⟦1⟧, ⟦2⟧, ⟦3⟧, ⟦4⟧, Crimea, Karelia and the Central Asian republics — with the odds rising the longer the war drags on (Ukraine and the Caucasus republics are the likeliest). A Karelian revolt also drags in ⟦5⟧.
